messages:
Caleb (AE): Quick sync request — customer Azimuth Labs wants a Private deployment POC. Their netops team mandates IP-based allowlists in their firewall and wants a prescriptive recommendation: PrivateLink vs Peering/TGW, exact firewall/ACL snippets we can hand them, and a conservative 3-week POC cost estimate (30k req/day, ~350GB). Can we draft a short, shareable note for them?

Yuna (NetEng): TL;DR: If they insist on stable IP allowlists, peering + controlled NAT with static EIPs on their side is the most straightforward. PrivateLink is faster to validate but ENI IPs are ephemeral — we can provide a snapshot for the POC window.

Sophie (Solutions): Timeline: PrivateLink validation typically 24-48 hrs if they can create vpce endpoints. Peering/TGW + stable EIP plan needs network change approvals and can add 3-10 business days. Recommend PrivateLink for PoC unless compliance requires immutable EIPs.

Mark (SecOps): Compliance note: For strict audit trails and FIPS/JIT allowlist policies, customers often prefer peering + egress through their own NAT/EIP so they can log a single source IP. We can support mTLS and cert rotation for either topology.

Yuna (NetEng): Firewalls (customer-side) — copyable snippet:
```
# PrivateLink (POC) - allow outbound to interface endpoint ENIs
allow proto tcp from <app-subnet-cidr> to <vpce-enis> port 443
# DNS + NTP
allow proto udp from <app-subnet-cidr> to <dns-resolver> port 53
allow proto udp from <app-subnet-cidr> to 0.0.0.0/0 port 123
# Optional health probes
allow proto tcp from <monitoring-subnet> to <vpce-enis> port 443

# Peering + NAT with static EIP (production)
allow proto tcp from <app-subnet-cidr> to <static-egress-eip> port 443
```
Best practice: use SGs on the interface endpoints and endpoint policies rather than hardcoding many IPs.

Sophie (Solutions): Security questionnaire one-liner we can give them: "Redwood supports AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) and VPC peering/Transit Gateway. TLS is enforced end-to-end and mutual TLS can be configured on request. For IP-only allowlisting, Redwood can provide ephemeral ENI IP snapshots during POCs; for stable allowlists we recommend peering with customer-controlled EIPs."

Caleb (AE): They also want a cost estimate for 3 weeks: 30k req/day -> ~350GB. Ballpark numbers? Need conservative range they can budget.

Sophie (Solutions): Ballpark POC cost components (PrivateLink):
- AWS: interface endpoint hours (~$0.01-0.03/endpoint-hour per AZ) + data processing (~$0.01-0.03/GB). For 350GB that implies ~$3.50-$10.50 in data processing, plus endpoint hours depending on AZ count (~$30-$150).
- Redwood: POC engineering/support time (network-heavy) typically $2k-$6k one-time.
- If peering + NAT/EIP: expect extra NAT hours and EIP charges (depends on cloud provider) and potential data transfer fees.

Give them a conservative all-in POC budget range: $2.5k - $7.5k (mostly professional time), excluding any cloud-native NAT/EIP charges they control.

Yuna (NetEng): Operational checklist (short):
1) Customer shares VPC CIDRs, AZs, and change windows.
2) Decide topology: PrivateLink for fast validation or Peering/TGW for stable EIPs.
3A) PrivateLink steps: we provide service name + AWS account IDs -> create interface endpoints per AZ -> attach SGs + endpoint policy -> allow outbound 443/DNS/NTP.
3B) Peering/TGW steps: exchange VPC IDs/roles, validate CIDR non-overlap, configure route tables + NAT with static EIPs, test.
4) If mTLS required, exchange certs and test handshake.
5) Run smoke tests (10 sample requests, latency check, error rates).
6) Capture redacted logs and TLS fingerprints for compliance.

ConnectBot: Created ticket AZ-PoC-2145 assigned to Yuna. Validation window scheduled Thu 15:00-15:30 UTC.

Mark (SecOps): We'll provide a short-lived ENI IP snapshot for their allowlist during the validation window — note in the SOW that ENI IPs are ephemeral and not recommended for production. If they need long-term IPs, recommend peering + their NAT EIPs.

Caleb (AE): Perfect. I'll send this as a single-page handoff to Azimuth Labs, include firewall snippet, checklist, and the conservative budget range. I'll also ask whether they prefer PrivateLink first. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
